steps.title: Sur lie
steps.body: Muscadet sur lie stays on its fine lees, the dead yeast, through winter until bottling in spring. This adds bread and yeasty notes, a creamier texture and protection against oxidation, plus a slight spritz from retained CO2. It gives a neutral grape more depth and character.

steps.title: Oysters
steps.body: Muscadet is the classic oyster wine: its high acidity, low alcohol and saline edge match shellfish perfectly. It also suits mussels, clams, crab, grilled sardines and beurre blanc, Nantes' butter sauce. Serve at 7 to 9 degrees. Most is best within three years; crus communaux age 10 years or more.

steps.prompt: What does sur lie ageing add to Muscadet?
options: Bread notes, creaminess and a slight spritz
steps.explanation: Lees contact adds texture and depth.

steps.body: Muscadet is one of the best-value white wines in France. A good sur lie with a dozen oysters is a classic French pleasure.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Sur lie ageing adds bread, cream and a slight spritz
Muscadet is the classic oyster wine
